### Summary

The caloric data of a card are given at a reference state: `u0_R` is the internal energy over $\mathcal R$ of a
species at the reference temperature `Tref`, and `s0_R` its entropy over $\mathcal R$ at `Tref` and the reference
pressure `Pref`. The latent heat of a phase change is not a separate input; it is the difference of the `u0_R`
values of vapour and condensate, and it must be positive for condensation to release energy. This section explains
how the offsets are shifted once, at construction, to $T = 0$ and to $T = 1\,\mathrm K$, $p = 1\,\mathrm{Pa}$ so that
every later formula is offset-free, why the card is warned about an endothermic condensate, and how the offsets have
to agree with the saturation curve of @sec-ch04 through the Clausius-Clapeyron relation.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Fix $u^\star_i$ and $s^\star_i$ from the card, @eq-ch03-reference-state-shift, and the latent heat
$\ell_j = -\sum_i \nu_{ij} u^\star_i$ that follows.

**Data.** `reference-state: {Tref, Pref}` [K, Pa] and per species `u0_R` [K], `s0_R` [-], `cv_R` [-]; in memory
`uref_R`, `sref_R`, `cref_R` after the shift.

**Placement.** Once, in `ThermoY::reset` or `ThermoX::reset`; guarded by the flag `offset_zero` so a cloned options
object is not shifted twice.

**Activation.** Always; defaults `Tref` $300\,\mathrm K$, `Pref` $10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}$, `u0_R` $0$, `s0_R` $0$. An
unknown key in `reference-state` is refused with a suggestion.

**Guarantee / limits.** The shift leaves $u_i(T)$ and $s_i(T, p)$ unchanged (exact algebra); a latent heat
$\le 0$ at `Tref` only warns.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below: `test_latent_heat_sign.py`, `test_reference_state_keys.py`.
:::

Local symbols: $T_\star$ and $p_\star$ the reference temperature and pressure (`Tref`, `Pref`); $u^\star_i$ and
$s^\star_i$ the stored offsets (`uref_R`, `sref_R`, as $u^\star_i/\mathcal R$ in K and $s^\star_i/\mathcal R$);
$\nu_{ij}$ the stoichiometric coefficient of species $i$ in reaction $j$, positive for products (`stoich`);
$\ell_j$ the molar latent heat of reaction $j$ [$\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$]; for the saturation curve the fit
parameters $\beta$, $\delta$, $T_r$, $p_r$ of the `ideal` form (@sec-ch04). The star marks the reference
state as the shared notation requires; the internal flag is `offset_zero`.

### Derivation

The card gives, per species, $\hat u_i(T_\star) =$ `u0_R` and $\hat s_i(T_\star, p_\star) =$ `s0_R` together with the
constant $\hat c_{v,i} =$ `cv_R`. With the baseline of @sec-ch03-caloric the energy at any temperature is
$\hat u_i(T) = \texttt{u0\_R} + \hat c_{v,i}(T - T_\star)$, and the entropy of a gas at any $(T, p)$ is
$\hat s_i = \texttt{s0\_R} + (\hat c_{v,i} + 1)\ln(T/T_\star) - \ln(p/p_\star)$. Collecting the constants gives the
offsets the code stores,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{u^\star_i}{\mathcal R} &= \texttt{u0\_R}_i - \hat c_{v,i}\,T_\star \quad \text{all species}, \\
\frac{s^\star_i}{\mathcal R} &= \texttt{s0\_R}_i - (\hat c_{v,i} + 1)\ln\max(T_\star, 1) + \ln\max(p_\star, 1) \quad (i < N_{\mathrm g}), \\
\frac{s^\star_i}{\mathcal R} &= 0 \quad (i \ge N_{\mathrm g}),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-reference-state-shift}
after which $\hat u_i(T) = u^\star_i/\mathcal R + \hat c_{v,i} T$ and $\hat s_i = s^\star_i/\mathcal R + (\hat c_{v,i}+1)\ln T - \ln p$
are the same functions as before (`[C1]`, `[C2]` of `reference_state_check.py`). @eq-ch03-reference-state-shift is
computed in `ThermoYImpl::reset` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_y.cpp ThermoYImpl::reset >}}) and identically in
`ThermoXImpl::reset` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::reset >}}). The clamps to $1$ let a card say
`Tref: 0.` (several test cards do) and mean "the offsets are already at $T = 0$", because $\ln 1 = 0$. The condensate
entropy offsets are set to zero because @sec-ch03-entropy derives the condensate entropy from the saturation curve
and never reads them. The flag `offset_zero` records that the shift has happened, so an options object shared by a
`ThermoX` and a `ThermoY`, or cloned, is shifted once.

The latent heat of reaction $j$ at the reference temperature is the energy released when the reaction proceeds by
one mole of extent, $\ell_j(T_\star) = -\mathcal R\sum_i \nu_{ij}\,\texttt{u0\_R}_i$, since $\nu_{ij} < 0$ for the
vapour consumed and $> 0$ for the condensate formed. The card loader evaluates this sum for every nucleation
reaction and warns when it is not positive:
$$
\ell_j(T_\star) = \mathcal R \Bigl(\sum_{i\,\in\,\mathrm{reactants}} |\nu_{ij}|\,\texttt{u0\_R}_i - \sum_{i\,\in\,\mathrm{products}} \nu_{ij}\,\texttt{u0\_R}_i\Bigr) \le 0
\;\Rightarrow\; \text{warning},
$$ {#eq-ch03-reference-state-latent}
and @eq-ch03-reference-state-latent is computed in `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}). For `tests/jupiter.yaml`,
$\mathrm{H_2O} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{H_2O(l)}$ has $\texttt{u0\_R} = 0$ and $-3430\,\mathrm K$, so
$\ell/\mathcal R = 3430\,\mathrm K$ ($28.5\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$); a condensate without `u0_R` gives $0$ and the
warning (`[C3]`).

The offsets are not free: they must agree with the saturation curve that @sec-ch04 uses, or the energy released by
condensation in the fixed-energy solver will not match the temperature dependence of the curve. For the `ideal`
curve $\ln p_{\mathrm{sat}} = \ln p_r + \beta(1 - T_r/T) - \delta\ln(T/T_r)$ and an ideal vapour over a condensate of
negligible volume, the Clausius-Clapeyron relation $\ell = \mathcal R T^2\,\mathrm d\ln p_{\mathrm{sat}}/\mathrm dT$ gives
$$
\ell(T) = \mathcal R\,(\beta T_r - \delta T),
$$ {#eq-ch03-reference-state-kirchhoff}
linear in $T$ with slope $-\mathcal R\delta = c_{p,v} - c_{c}$: the Kirchhoff form (`[C4]`). With the baseline
enthalpies $\hat h_v - \hat h_c = (u^\star_v - u^\star_c)/\mathcal R + (\hat c_{v,v} + 1 - \hat c_{v,c})\,T$, a
consistent card therefore has $\delta = \hat c_{v,c} - \hat c_{v,v} - 1$ and $\beta T_r = (u^\star_v - u^\star_c)/\mathcal R$.
The Jupiter test card uses the `h2o_ideal` constants ($\beta = 24.845$, $T_r = 273.16\,\mathrm K$, $\delta = 4.986$)
with $\hat c_{v,c} - \hat c_{v,v} - 1 = 9 - 2.5 - 1 = 5.5$ and $(u^\star_v - u^\star_c)/\mathcal R = 5380\,\mathrm K$
against $\beta T_r = 6787\,\mathrm K$: it is *not* Kirchhoff-consistent, and its moist adiabats carry that
inconsistency (@sec-ch03-adiabat). Two cards in the tree are consistent by construction: `h2o_bryan`, whose $\beta$
is chosen so that $\ell(273.15\,\mathrm K) = 2.5\times10^6\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$ (`[C5]`, reproducing the literal
$24.815845$ of {{< code src/vapors/vapor_functions.h h2o_bryan >}}), and `examples/jupiter_kcl_mgsio3.yaml`, whose
`u0_R` values are $-B\ln 10$ for curves of the form $\ln(10)(A - B/T)$ with $\Delta c_p = 0$ (`[C6]`). The check
`reference_state_check.py` holds all six statements.

### Numerical method

There is no discretisation in this section; @fig-ch03-reference-state-offsets shows what the shift does to the two
energy lines of water in the Jupiter card. The order of operations at construction is: read the card, form the
species groups (@sec-ch03-species-state), copy `cv_R`, `u0_R`, `s0_R` into `cref_R`, `uref_R`, `sref_R` in group
order, then shift once in `reset`. A `ThermoY` and a `ThermoX` built from the same options object share the shifted
arrays. The latent-heat sum is evaluated on the *unshifted* `u0_R`, which is the same as on the shifted $u^\star_i$
only when the heat capacities of vapour and condensate are equal; the warning therefore tests the latent heat at
$T_\star$, as its message says.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-reference-state-offsets
#| fig-cap: "Molar internal energy over the gas constant of water vapour (blue) and liquid water (dashed green) with the constant heat capacities of the Jupiter test card. The card gives the offsets at the reference temperature of 300 K (circles; the vertical vermillion bar is the latent heat there, 3430 K); the code stores the intercepts at zero temperature (squares), which are the same two lines."
#| fig-alt: "Two straight lines of internal energy against temperature from 0 to 400 K: the vapour line with slope 2.5 passing through zero at 300 K, and the steeper liquid line with slope 9 passing through minus 3430 K at 300 K. Markers show the intercepts at zero temperature, minus 750 K and minus 6130 K, and a vertical bar at 300 K marks the gap of 3430 K between the lines."
#| echo: false
```

: Code map of the reference state. {#tbl-ch03-reference-state-code}

Walk-through:

1. `check_reference_state` ({{< code src/species.cpp check_reference_state >}}) accepts an empty block (defaults
   kept), refuses a list or a scalar (`must be a map of key: value pairs`) and refuses any key outside `Tref`,
   `Pref`, `use-nasa9-cp`, `use-h2-cp`, `h2-cp-mode`, naming the closest one (`did you mean`).
2. `ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml` returns a null options object when the block is absent altogether: a card without
   `reference-state` has no thermodynamics.
3. After the reactions are registered, the latent-heat loop warns per reaction with the text `has latent heat ... K <= 0
   at Tref, i.e. condensation absorbs energy. Set u0_R (u/R at Tref) on the condensate`.
4. `reset` of either module shifts once and prints the shifted arrays when `verbose` is on.

A card fragment that satisfies all of the above and is Kirchhoff-consistent with its curve (a YAML card; the fence
is left untyped until the key registry of the glossary carries these keys):

```text
reference-state: {Tref: 0., Pref: 1.e5}
species:
  - {name: dry, composition: {N: 1.56, O: 0.42}, cv_R: 2.5}
  - {name: H2O, composition: {H: 2, O: 1}, cv_R: 2.5, u0_R: 0.}
  - {name: H2O(l), composition: {H: 2, O: 1}, cv_R: 8.486009, u0_R: -6786.66}
reactions:
  - {equation: H2O <=> H2O(l), type: nucleation, rate-constant: {formula: h2o_bryan}}
```

Here $\hat c_{v,c} - \hat c_{v,v} - 1 = 4.986009 = \delta$ and $u^\star_v - u^\star_c = 6786.66\,\mathrm K \approx \beta T_r
= 24.815845 \times 273.16\,\mathrm K$, as @eq-ch03-reference-state-kirchhoff requires.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The Kirchhoff consistency of @eq-ch03-reference-state-kirchhoff is not checked at load. `tests/jupiter.yaml`
  violates it by about $20\,\%$ in $\beta T_r$, and nothing warns; the fixed-energy solver of @sec-ch04
  then releases the card's latent heat while the saturation curve moves with the fit's, so the equilibrium
  temperature it reaches is that of an inconsistent substance. Not measured: the temperature error this causes.
- The latent-heat warning is a warning, not an error, and is evaluated at `Tref` only; a latent heat that changes
  sign at another temperature (large $\delta$) is not reported.
- `s0_R` of a condensate is read and then zeroed; a card that sets it has no effect.
- The entropy offsets are shifted only for gases, with `Tref` and `Pref` clamped to $1$; a card with
  $0 < T_\star < 1\,\mathrm K$ is shifted as if $T_\star = 1\,\mathrm K$, silently.
:::
